Phase 3 (#1579) progress. Two defects found and fixed; the five checks are not yet quotable.

**Fleet delivery.** Forced via Shepherd's scheduler (`wake: claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/fleet-baseline`), which filed Shepherd `#411` and followed each member to current. **12 of 13 converged**; `missingbulb/googlecalendareventcreator` did not and the item parked `needs-human`. **Finding 1 — `update` would have fired on the canon (fixed, #1593).** Converting `update` to `['none']` removed the `stamp.present` condition, which was the only thing keeping the task off a repo with no vendored mount. The design's answer is settings-level disablement, and the canon's own entry was never written. Its board (#1130) recorded the old decline at this morning's anchor:

```
claudinite-lifecycle/update | daily | 2026-09-02T05:00:00.000Z | no |
no vendored mount (no installed versions) — nothing to update
```

From tomorrow's 05:00 anchor it would have filed a daily item with nothing to converge.

**Finding 2 — `disabledTasks` was rejected by the settings validator (fixed, #1593).** #1583 added the key to the planner but not to `SCHEDULE_KEYS` in `repo-context.mjs`, so `loadConfig` failed it as an unknown key. The one setting the design names as the answer to repo shape could not be used by *any* repo. Caught by CI on #1593, not locally — my pre-commit run there was `check_the_work` only, which does not cover the world scope.

⚠️ **The validator fix does not reach members yet.** The engine ships only at a bumped `ENGINE_VERSION`, and a bump requires the canary rehearsal. **The five reads are still pending**, deliberately not forced:

- Checks 1 and 2 (a movement-gated task declining on a quiet window, then running on an active one) — the board currently evaluates `go` for all four candidates, so a forced wake would start a real opus session and open a PR rather than demonstrate a decline.
- Check 5 (a `Claudinite-Task:`-stamped commit not satisfying `substantive-change`) — not observable yet: no task has delivered anything since the trailer existed, so there is nothing stamped to test against.

All three resolve on their own at tomorrow's 05:00 anchor, which also produces the first post-change board rows.

## Why this could not be watched now

#1511 changed three things inside the flow **every member runs on every nightly converge**:

- `write` now stages a path under `.github/workflows/` instead of dropping it.
- The flow announces `CLAUDINITE_CAN_WITHHOLD_WORKFLOWS`, so records naming a workflow path stop skipping themselves.
- The staging sweep is scoped to files the current run did not stage, where it previously cleared the directory unconditionally.

The unit tests prove each in isolation against a synthetic member tree. What they cannot prove is that a real member — with its own declaration, its own pack set, its own drift — still converges green through the changed flow. `pack-update.mjs` is vendored verbatim, so a regression here is a regression on all 13 at once, and the failure would look like members quietly falling behind rather than anything red here.

The second half of `Verify:` is the sharper one. **Nothing currently materializes or rewrites a workflow path** — the record that will is deliberately held back (see #1509's tail, and the follow-up issue). So the correct observation today is that the lane is open and *idle*: any file appearing under `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` means the flow is staging something no record asked for, which would be a defect in the `write` change rather than a delivery.

The worker resolves its flows against a **fresh canon clone at HEAD**, not the member's own mount:

```js
git(['clone', '--depth', '1', CANON_URL, tmp]);
const load = async (rel) => import(pathToFileURL(join(tmp, rel)).href);

on each member's default branch — every one must call `load('packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/…')`. A member still on the old spelling has not converged past #1352 yet, and deleting the tree strands it.

That gate is met only after every member converges to `claudinite-lifecycle 60824.6` or higher, so the check is worth making after the fleet has had a night.

- Delete `updates/` whole — `engine-update.mjs`, `pack-update.mjs`, `terminals.mjs`, `install.mjs`, `legacy-entry.mjs`, `README.md`.

## What this proves

The whole point of the change: the scheduler was **71% of private Actions spend** at ~26 min/day per member, because Actions bills each job rounded up and the cron fired 24 times a day to do about 13 minutes of work. Two ticks a day should make that ~2 min/day. Nothing so far has measured a real repo — only the simulator.

## What makes this step's world ready

#1235 closed (every member on the new cron), **and** at least one full UTC day has elapsed since, so there is a complete day to count.

## What to observe

For each **private** member — the ones that cost anything; public repos are free and unlimited:

1. **The count.** Scheduler workflow runs for one complete UTC day. Expect exactly **2**. Baseline: 24.
2. **Nothing was dropped.** No task's standing item is missing its occurrence for that day — a cheaper cron that quietly stopped instantiating work is a regression, not a saving.
3. **The risk the simulator could not model.** A whole day's chain now settles serially inside one executor run. Read the longest executor run's duration against the workflow's `timeout-minutes: 350`. The simulator's task durations are fixtures, so this is the first real read of whether a member's day actually fits.

## What counts as this step having worked

Every private member shows 2 scheduler runs for the measured day, no missing occurrences, and no executor run near its timeout.

## When the check fails

Comment what you read and **leave this issue open** — closing releases the next link.

- Still 24 runs on some member → its workflow never landed; reopen #1235's question there rather than proceeding.
- Missing occurrences → this is a real regression in the cadence change. Reopen #1225 with what is missing and stop the chain.
- An executor run near the timeout → do **not** fail the step, but say so plainly on #1225: it is the residual risk the plan named, and it wants its own issue rather than silence.

## How it ends

Comment the per-member figures on #1225 — runs/day before and after, and the longest executor run — then close this issue as completed. That close releases Link 3.

* gcec tasks: declare the outcome/automerge pair, scoped by a pack merge rule

`create-extractor` said `open-pr` and meant "a human always reviews the
extraction": that is `pr` + `automerge: 'nothing'`, now spelled as such.

`generic-extractor-improvements` said `merged-pr`, which normalizes to
`automerge: 'anything'` — an unreviewed merge of any diff, including one the
routine's own postconditions.sh would have rejected. Its real ceiling is that
postcondition's four-path scope, so the pack declares it once as the
`generic-coverage-scope` merge rule and the task names it. A win in the generic
extractor, its helpers, the covering test and the regenerated artifacts lands as
before; a custom/.js, the manifest, or a deleted helper parks for review.

The scope pattern now exists as a shell literal and a JSON regex, which cannot
share a constant — postconditions.sh runs where no engine is loaded, and the
policy engine judges a branch it never checked out. The new blocking
`generic-coverage-scope-agrees` check compares the two byte-for-byte, so
widening one alone cannot pass.

Refs #1101

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KLncjMZm1eMBFAq65Kzobz

* Pin the create-extractor contract as the outcome/automerge pair

The declaration test asserted the retired `open-pr` spelling, so it failed the
moment the ceiling was restated. It now pins both halves — a run may open a PR,
and nothing it produces may land without a person — which is what the assertion
was there to protect.

fileDescriptions' two task rows were describing neither declaration correctly
(`hourly` was retired long ago, and the weekly routine's ceiling was never
`open-pr`); both rows are re-derived from the declarations as they now read.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KLncjMZm1eMBFAq65Kzobz

* Drop the RULES.md bullet the scope check already covers

The bullet described where the two scope patterns live and that a check
compares them — how the repo works, which is not what RULES.md is for. It was
also the only bullet in the file naming a check by id, against the pack's own
convention: npm-test-glob-coverage has no bullet at all, and the neighbouring
generic-coverage entry explicitly leaves mechanics to "the gate's own headers".

The blocking check needs no prose companion. It names both files, prints both
literals and states the fix at the moment an agent widens one of them, which is
strictly better than a paragraph read at session start.

Root cause found, and it predates my change entirely.

The 11:00 run **did** execute `claudinite-lifecycle/update`, and its log shows what happened:

```
update: merged PR #1138 — its pull_request run is parked at action_required (never ran)
        while the dispatched run passed — check Settings → Actions → General →
        workflow-approval requirements
update: landed PR #1138; main has moved past this checkout — next cycle converges from it
#1139: task:status:done
```

That's `disposeOpenPull` returning `merged`: the cycle found a **stale incumbent update PR** from an earlier cycle, merged it, and correctly ended — a converge computed from a checkout that main has moved past would re-deliver a diff already landed. So the run spent itself clearing the backlog and never converged to canon's new versions. The stamp confirms it: still `claudinite-tasks 60901.2`, i.e. the versions that old PR carried.

The underlying cause is in that same line: this repo's `pull_request` runs park at `action_required` under a workflow-approval requirement, so its update PRs never land on their own and pile up. Nothing to do with preconditions — it would have behaved identically yesterday.

The log states the remedy itself: *next cycle converges from it*. The incumbent is gone, so a second wake should now converge properly.

`missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator` investigated. **Its update did not fail, and my change is not involved.**

What actually happened, from its own executor log at 11:00:

```
code_work claudinite-lifecycle/update [#1139]

        while the dispatched run passed — check Settings → Actions → General →
        workflow-approval requirements

#1139: task:status:done
```

The task ran, succeeded, and closed `task:status:done`. It hit `disposeOpenPull`'s `merged` branch: it found a **stale incumbent update PR** left over from an earlier cycle, merged it, and then correctly ended the cycle — converging from a checkout that main has already moved past would re-deliver a diff that has landed. So the whole cycle went on clearing the backlog, and canon's new versions were never vendored. Its stamp confirms exactly that, still carrying the versions that old PR delivered:

```
basics 60901.5 · chrome-extension 60901.1 · claudinite-growth 60901.3
claudinite-lifecycle 60901.2 · claudinite-tasks 60901.2
product-wiki 60830.3 · tidy-repo 60830.3        (engine 60823.1)
```

The root cause is named in that same log line and is a **repo setting, not code**: this repo's `pull_request` runs park at `action_required` under a workflow-approval requirement, so its update PRs never land on their own. They accumulate, and each forced cycle is spent disposing of one instead of converging. It would have behaved identically yesterday — the fleet sweep's 20-minute follow simply expired while it was doing backlog work.

I've re-woken its `update` (the log's own stated remedy: *next cycle converges from it*) and I'm waiting to confirm the stamp actually moves — a dispatch is not a result.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

{"number":1572,"title":"Declarative task preconditions + the repo-active silence gate","body":"Give the task contract a declarative `preconditions` field — a **conjunction of positively-named conditions** evaluated over the collected signals — with a built-in term vocabulary, task-local terms for task-specific gates, and a standard silence discipline: no task runs on a silent repo unless its declaration visibly says so, where a scheduled task's own PRs and commits count as silence.

Design (end state + rationale): `docs/task-preconditions/DESIGN.md` (PR #1574).

Decisions taken through the design reviews:
- The list is `&&` (`['X', 'Y || Z']` = `X && (Y || Z)`); `||` joins alternatives inside a term; `none` (sole entry) is the empty precondition. The comma deliberately opposes automerge's union — one field grants, the other requires — and the contrast is stated in the doc.
- No veto terms, no exemption markers, no `precondition_context`, no comments above the declaration: conditions are positively named and self-describing.
- Extensibility is task-local: a task-specific gate is a named term in `preconditions.mjs` beside its `task.mjs` (`log-past-retention`, `manifest-ahead`, `fleet-local-packs-changed`, `request-eligible`); built-ins (~11, including the generic `commits-under:`/`commits-outside:` pair) live in `precondition-policy.mjs`. The canon carries no `precondition` functions; the legacy function field stays accepted for member-local files forever.
- Repo-shape gates are not preconditions: `taskScheduler.disabledTasks` in `.claudinite-settings.json` disables a task the repo doesn't want, read by the scheduler before instantiation.
- `precondition_signals` is derived from the expression; unresolvable terms/signals `{ error }` loudly, never a quiet decline.
- Task output is classified silent structurally, via a `Claudinite-Task: /` commit trailer stamped by the delivery lanes.
- Migration is near-zero by construction: `preconditions` is a new property beside the old one, validation is exactly-one-of, the vendor set delivers engine+packs atomically, and nothing forces member-local files to convert — so there is no fleet migration record and no cleanup phase.

Not-before: 7 days after #1579 closes

Judge the element against the design's expectations, from its real record (the queue's closed work items, the usage-fold aggregate, the scheduler run logs over the week):

- [ ] **Did the silence gate do its job?** Count declined runs of `rule-revalidation`, `prose-to-checks-sweep` and `wiki-growth` on quiet windows vs the same tasks' unconditional firings in the week before the cutover. Expectation: on a quiet repo these three stop spending model runs entirely; on an active repo their cadence is unchanged.
- [ ] **Did anything starve wrongly?** Any task that never fired all week whose subject did move — read its decline reasons, not just its silence. Expectation: none; the loud-error lane (not quiet declines) catches evaluator faults.
- [ ] **Do the composed reasons read?** Sample a handful of item comments: does a term-composed reason tell a human why the run happened/declined without opening the task file? Expectation: yes — that was the readability goal.
- [ ] **Is the vocabulary the right size?** Any task-local term that a second task now wants (promote to built-in), any built-in no declaration uses (drop), any `precondition` function that crept back into the canon. Expectation: built-ins ≈ 11, task-local ≈ 4, canon functions 0.
- [ ] **Misuse check**: any `preconditions: ['none']` on a task whose subject is actually repo movement, added since the cutover.

  freq=$(grep -oE "frequency: *'[^']+'" "$f" | head -1 | sed "s/frequency: *//")
  pre=$(grep -oE "preconditions: *\[[^]]*\]" "$f" | head -1 | sed 's/preconditions: *//')
  printf '%-52s %-12s %s\n' "$name" "$freq" "$pre"
done

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. - extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. - file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and author the canon packs those facets earn. Use from a canon when a project's evidence shows a facet its shelf does not yet home — the curation stages' pack-writing method, and an owner's when asking what a project has taught the shelf.

- improve-comments: Improve the comments in a repo's own source — delete the ones that restate the code or narrate a past edit, correct the ones that have drifted from what the code now does, and add the why where only a reader's guess carries it. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

{"number":1578,"title":"Implement the preconditions evaluator and convert the canon","body":"Phase 2 of #1572 — the whole implementation, written as one stacked pass and reviewed once. The end state is `docs/task-preconditions/DESIGN.md` (merged by [#1574](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1574)); this issue only lists the work.

- [ ] **Evaluator** — `packs/claudinite-tasks/precondition-policy.mjs` beside `merge-policy.mjs`: parse (conjunction list, `||` within a term, `none` sole-entry, inline `:`), the built-in term set from the design's table, task-local term resolution from `tasks//preconditions.mjs` (flat namespace, collision loud), derived `precondition_signals`, composed reason/context, `{ error }` on unknown/unreadable — never a quiet decline.
- [ ] **Contract + checks** — `task-contract.mjs` accepts exactly one of `preconditions` / `precondition`; `task-declaration-shape` validates the expression statically; executor + scheduler evaluate either form at the one pick point.
- [ ] **Silence classification** — delivery lanes (`land-pr.mjs`, `deliver-generated.mjs`, the queue's PR delivery) stamp `Claudinite-Task: /`; the non-task movement terms read it (one commit read per in-window PR), keeping the existing bot/housekeeping/corpus-only exclusions for pre-trailer history.
- [ ] **Settings disablement** — `taskScheduler.disabledTasks: ['/']`, read by the scheduler before instantiating; replaces the retired repo-shape gates (store-release's pipeline probe, growth-dedup's local-packs probe, the fleet-token probes).
- [ ] **Convert the canon** — all 25 declarations per the design's conversion table (including the four task-local `preconditions.mjs`: `log-past-retention`, `manifest-ahead`, `fleet-local-packs-changed`, `request-eligible`); pack version bumps + VERSIONS.md rows + catalog rows.
- [ ] **Tests** — see-it-fail per term and per grammar rule; the sim/scenario suites green; a fixture proving the conjunction (`['X', 'Y || Z']` = `X && (Y || Z)`) and the either-or contract validation.

Exit: full suite green (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`), `task-declaration-shape` green over the real tree, one reviewed PR stack merged.

Migration cost is deliberately near-zero: `preconditions` is a new property, `precondition` functions stay accepted forever (member-local task files never converge), and a member's engine and packs travel in one vendor set — so there is no fleet migration record, no skew window, and no cleanup phase.","state":"closed","state_reason":"completed","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1578","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","assignees":[],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-09-01T17:40:20Z","updated_at":"2026-09-02T10:52:12Z","closed_at":"2026-09-02T10:52:12Z","closed_by":"missingbulb","has_parent":true,"has_children":false,"parent":{"number":1572,"title":"Declarative task preconditions + the repo-active silence gate","state":"OPEN","url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1572","repository":"missingbulb/Claudinite"},"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":1,"references":[{"number":1583,"title":"Declarative task preconditions, and the repo-active silence gate","state":"MERGED","url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1583","repository":"missingbulb/Claudinite"}]}}

input.body:
Phase 3 of #1572, runnable only once #1578's stack has merged and the nightly converge has delivered it.

Blocked-by: #1578
Not-before: 2026-09-09

**Ready when**: the canon's own scheduler runs carry the new evaluator (the head sha's scheduler run log names `precondition-policy`), and at least one member's stamp shows the bumped `claudinite-tasks` version.

**What counts as this step having worked** (each read from a real run, quoted on #1572):
- [ ] A movement-gated task (`tidy-issues` or `growth-extract`) declines on a quiet window with a term-composed reason, via a forced scheduler wake (`workflow_dispatch` with `wake` naming the task) — the wake-that-finds-no-work verdict, not a failure.
- [ ] The same task runs on a window with real activity, its item's Context carrying the term-contributed scope.
- [x] A `['none']` task (`task-janitor`) runs unconditionally as before. — read on #1598, quoted on #1572.
- [ ] A task-local term evaluates (`logs-prune` declines or fires on the age arithmetic, reason quoting the ages). — **scoped down**: the canon leaves `retention_days` unset, so the live read available here is the term's unset-retention decline, not the age branch. input.body:
Give the task contract a declarative `preconditions` field — a **conjunction of positively-named conditions** evaluated over the collected signals — with a built-in term vocabulary, task-local terms for task-specific gates, and a standard silence discipline: no task runs on a silent repo unless its declaration visibly says so, where a scheduled task's own PRs and commits count as silence.

Design (end state + rationale): `docs/task-preconditions/DESIGN.md` (PR #1574).

Decisions taken through the design reviews:
- The list is `&&` (`['X', 'Y || Z']` = `X && (Y || Z)`); `||` joins alternatives inside a term; `none` (sole entry) is the empty precondition. The comma deliberately opposes automerge's union — one field grants, the other requires — and the contrast is stated in the doc.
- No veto terms, no exemption markers, no `precondition_context`, no comments above the declaration: conditions are positively named and self-describing.
- Extensibility is task-local: a task-specific gate is a named term in `preconditions.mjs` beside its `task.mjs` (`log-past-retention`, `manifest-ahead`, `fleet-local-packs-changed`, `request-eligible`); built-ins (~11, including the generic `commits-under:`/`commits-outside:` pair) live in `precondition-policy.mjs`. The canon carries no `precondition` functions; the legacy function field stays accepted for member-local files forever.
- Repo-shape gates are not preconditions: `taskScheduler.disabledTasks` in `.claudinite-settings.json` disables a task the repo doesn't want, read by the scheduler before instantiation.
- `precondition_signals` is derived from the expression; unresolvable terms/signals `{ error }` loudly, never a quiet decline.
- Task output is classified silent structurally, via a `Claudinite-Task: <pack>/<task>` commit trailer stamped by the delivery lanes.
- Migration is near-zero by construction: `preconditions` is a new property beside the old one, validation is exactly-one-of, the vendor set delivers engine+packs atomically, and nothing forces member-local files to convert — so there is no fleet migration record and no cleanup phase.

## Plan

No phase-zero out-of-band setup: every step is in-repo code; no new secret, permission or platform setting.

- [x] **Phase 1 — design doc.** #1573, merged by PR #1574.
- [x] **Phase 2 — implement + convert.** #1578 — evaluator, contract, trailer, settings disablement, all 25 conversions, tests; one stacked review pass. Merged by PR #1583, with #1593 fixing the two regressions it carried.
- [ ] **Phase 3 — validate live.** #1579 (`Not-before: 2026-09-09`) — five quoted reads off real anchored runs. Read 3 quoted; four pending real windows.
- [ ] **Phase 4 — retrospective.** #1580 (Blocked-by #1579, not before ~a week live) — silence-gate savings, starvation check, reason readability, vocabulary size; closes the tracker.

`create-extractor` said `open-pr` and meant "a human always reviews the
extraction": that is `pr` + `automerge: 'nothing'`, now spelled as such.

`generic-extractor-improvements` said `merged-pr`, which normalizes to
`automerge: 'anything'` — an unreviewed merge of any diff, including one the
routine's own postconditions.sh would have rejected. Its real ceiling is that
postcondition's four-path scope, so the pack declares it once as the
`generic-coverage-scope` merge rule and the task names it. A win in the generic
extractor, its helpers, the covering test and the regenerated artifacts lands as
before; a custom/.js, the manifest, or a deleted helper parks for review.

The scope pattern now exists as a shell literal and a JSON regex, which cannot
share a constant — postconditions.sh runs where no engine is loaded, and the
policy engine judges a branch it never checked out. The new blocking
`generic-coverage-scope-agrees` check compares the two byte-for-byte, so
widening one alone cannot pass.

The declaration was never written for this repo. The vendor set ships the pack's

names are unchanged too, regenerated from this repo's own declarations.

name: Tests

on:
  # Manual runs from the Actions tab / API, on any branch. GitHub only exposes
  # this once the workflow is on the default branch, so it covers future dev
  # branches; for a brand-new branch, the push trigger below runs CI right away.
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    # main, plus agent dev branches, so CI (including the real-Chrome e2e smoke
    # test) runs on a dev branch without opening a PR. A branch that also has an
    # open PR gets a pull_request run too — accepted as minor duplication.
    branches: [main, "claude/**"]
    # A page recorded by the gcec record-page / create-extractor tasks only touches
    # dev/requirements/extractor/data/; ignoring that path keeps a bare recording
    # from re-triggering this workflow. (UI snapshots have no recorder — they're
    # regenerated by hand — so a commit that changes them SHOULD run CI to validate
    # them.)
    paths-ignore:
      - "dev/requirements/extractor/data/**"

# GitHub's implicit run shell is bash -e without pipefail, so a failing piped
# command still shows the step green. Force pipefail for every run: step.
defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Validate extension manifest.json
        run: node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('extension/manifest.json'))"

      # "For me" tests: deterministic, no network. These gate every change.
      - name: Run offline tests
        run: npm run test:offline

      # "For you" tests: the reviewed assertions, run against the cached
      # HTML files committed to dev/requirements/extractor/data/ (recorded by the
      # gcec record-page / create-extractor tasks — this job does not fetch them).
      - name: Run live tests
        run: npm run test:live

      # Renders each dev/requirements/<kind>/cases/*.case.js through the popup's real render() and
      # compares it to the committed dev/requirements/<kind>/cases/*.png (browsable on GitHub).
      # Deterministic and dependency-light (satori + resvg, no browser), so it
      # runs alongside the other tests.
      - name: Run UI snapshot test
        run: npm run test:ui

      # Real-Chrome smoke test: loads the unpacked extension and asserts the MV3
      # service worker registers — the one layer that exercises Chrome's actual
      # extension loader, the layer that broke in #146. The test itself has no
      # npm dependency (it drives Chrome over the DevTools Protocol via Node's
      # built-in WebSocket). Two environment quirks handled here:
      #   * branded Chrome 137+ dropped the --load-extension switch, so we fetch
      #     Chrome for Testing via `npx @puppeteer/browsers` (run on demand, not
      #     a project dependency — nothing added to package.json/the lockfile);
      #   * MV3 extensions only load in *headful* Chrome, so it runs under xvfb.
      # Separate from the browserless suites above; the test skips if no Chrome.
      #
      # The Chrome for Testing download (~150 MB) is cached to keep CI fast. The
      # key rolls monthly so the cache is reused on virtually every run, while
      # still refreshing to a current Chrome often enough to catch Chrome changes
      # (the whole point of this layer).
      - name: Chrome for Testing cache key
        id: cft-key
        run: echo "key=cft-${{ runner.os }}-$(date -u +%Y-%m)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Cache Chrome for Testing
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/cft
          key: ${{ steps.cft-key.outputs.key }}
      - name: Run real-Chrome extension-load smoke test
        run: |
          # Reuse the cached binary when present; otherwise fetch Chrome for Testing.
          # mkdir first: on a cache MISS the directory does not exist, and under this
          # workflow's `bash -e -o pipefail` a `find` on a missing path exits 1 and
          # kills the step — before the fallback below, which exists precisely to
          # handle a cache miss, can run. Redirecting stderr hides the message, not
          # the exit status. The monthly key roll made that the first run of a month.
          mkdir -p "${RUNNER_TEMP}/cft"
          CHROME_PATH="$(find "${RUNNER_TEMP}/cft" -type f -name chrome 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
          if [ -z "$CHROME_PATH" ]; then
            out="$(npx --yes @puppeteer/browsers install chrome@stable --path "${RUNNER_TEMP}/cft")"
            echo "$out"
            CHROME_PATH="$(echo "$out" | tail -n1 | awk '{print $NF}')"
          fi
          export CHROME_PATH
          echo "Using Chrome at: $CHROME_PATH"
          xvfb-run --auto-servernum npm run test:e2e

* gcec tasks: declare the outcome/automerge pair, scoped by a pack merge rule

`create-extractor` said `open-pr` and meant "a human always reviews the
extraction": that is `pr` + `automerge: 'nothing'`, now spelled as such.

`generic-extractor-improvements` said `merged-pr`, which normalizes to
`automerge: 'anything'` — an unreviewed merge of any diff, including one the
routine's own postconditions.sh would have rejected. Its real ceiling is that
postcondition's four-path scope, so the pack declares it once as the
`generic-coverage-scope` merge rule and the task names it. A win in the generic
extractor, its helpers, the covering test and the regenerated artifacts lands as
before; a custom/.js, the manifest, or a deleted helper parks for review.

The scope pattern now exists as a shell literal and a JSON regex, which cannot
share a constant — postconditions.sh runs where no engine is loaded, and the
policy engine judges a branch it never checked out. The new blocking
`generic-coverage-scope-agrees` check compares the two byte-for-byte, so
widening one alone cannot pass.

Refs #1101

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KLncjMZm1eMBFAq65Kzobz

* Pin the create-extractor contract as the outcome/automerge pair

The declaration test asserted the retired `open-pr` spelling, so it failed the
moment the ceiling was restated. It now pins both halves — a run may open a PR,
and nothing it produces may land without a person — which is what the assertion
was there to protect.

fileDescriptions' two task rows were describing neither declaration correctly
(`hourly` was retired long ago, and the weekly routine's ceiling was never
`open-pr`); both rows are re-derived from the declarations as they now read.

Refs #1101

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KLncjMZm1eMBFAq65Kzobz

* Drop the RULES.md bullet the scope check already covers

The bullet described where the two scope patterns live and that a check
compares them — how the repo works, which is not what RULES.md is for. It was
also the only bullet in the file naming a check by id, against the pack's own
convention: npm-test-glob-coverage has no bullet at all, and the neighbouring
generic-coverage entry explicitly leaves mechanics to "the gate's own headers".

The blocking check needs no prose companion. It names both files, prints both
literals and states the fix at the moment an agent widens one of them, which is
strictly better than a paragraph read at session start.

Refs #1101

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5

content.text:
Confirmed, and it reverses my diagnosis completely. For PR [#1141](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/pull/1141)'s head sha `a224a8b2`, there are **two** runs of the same `Tests` workflow:

| Run | Event | Created | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| [33627800418](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/actions/runs/33627800418) | `workflow_dispatch` | 12:02:58 | **success** 12:03:57 |
| — | PR merged | | 12:03:58 |
| [33627802053](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/actions/runs/33627802053) | `pull_request` | 12:02:59 | failure 12:04:00, **0 jobs** |

The lane behaves exactly as `land-pr.mjs` documents: it dispatches its own run because a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push emits no CI, waits for that to go green, then merges. GitHub *also* auto-created a `pull_request` run; the merge deletes the branch a second later and that duplicate dies as a startup failure. Same pattern on `bf80bd66` and `c64cc431` — every red `pull_request` run has a green `workflow_dispatch` twin on the identical sha.

**So there is no workflow-approval setting to fix.** Three things I told you earlier were wrong, and I'd rather say so directly:

- Not `action_required` — the runs complete, they don't park.
- No PR backlog — zero open update PRs; every `claudinite/update-*` branch is gone.
- Updates are not merging unverified — CI runs green on every one, just under a different event.

What's left is real but cosmetic: roughly half of gcec's Actions tab is red for runs that never executed a job. That noise is what sent me to the wrong conclusion twice, so it isn't free — but it's a canon-wide question, since any member whose CI answers both `pull_request` and `workflow_dispatch` produces the same orphan.

questions.question: There is no gcec setting to fix — the red runs are orphaned duplicates of green ones. Worth fixing the noise, and where?

options.label: Cancel the orphan in the canon (Recommended)
options.description: After landDelivery merges, have it cancel any in-flight pull_request run on the same sha. One API call, fleet-wide, no member repo changes. Red becomes grey 'cancelled' — honest, since the run genuinely was abandoned.

options.label: Leave it — it's cosmetic
options.description: The merges are verified and nothing is blocked. Accept the red noise in the Actions tab; no code changes anywhere.

options.label: Skip the duplicate in gcec's test.yml
options.description: Add a job-level `if:` that skips the pull_request run on claudinite/* branches. Fixes gcec only; every other member keeps producing orphans, and it's CI plumbing copied per-repo rather than owned centrally.

options.label: Investigate first, decide after
options.description: Open an issue to work out whether the dispatch is even needed where GitHub already creates a pull_request run, rather than papering over the duplicate.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and author the canon packs those facets earn. Use from a canon when a project's evidence shows a facet its shelf does not yet home — the curation stages' pack-writing method, and an owner's when asking what a project has taught the shelf.
- git-github-advanced: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the baseline lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- improve-comments: Improve the comments in a repo's own source — delete the ones that restate the code or narrate a past edit, correct the ones that have drifted from what the code now does, and add the why where only a reader's guess carries it. Use when working a repo's comments as their own pass (the tidy-repo pack's improve-comments task), never as a side effect of another change.
- merge-to-main: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
- production-retrospective: Design and file the review that comes back on its own once a larger element has lived in production long enough to judge — is it working, misused, overused, underused — read from its real production record against expectations written down when the element was designed. Use when designing a larger element (the brief is authored then), when filing a migration plan's chain (the retrospective is its last link), when a merge completes a design-doc'd element, or when defining a new retrospective class for a pack, a repo, or the fleet.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).

Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.

Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-pack-prose: How pack prose is written — RULES.md rules, SKILL.md bodies and check text in a Claudinite pack, local or canon — brevity, structure, triggerability, findability, and the per-pack references doc that carries each rule's rationale. Use before writing or editing any pack's RULES.md or SKILL.md, or when landing a lesson as prose.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. content.text:
Confirmed on evidence, then the review.

**Your premise holds.** All 25 tasks declare `preconditions` in the current grammar; zero occurrences of the retired `precondition_signals` (or any other legacy gate field) anywhere under `packs/*/tasks/`. Nothing left over.

## The structural fact that reframes the question

**There is nothing per-repo to align.** Preconditions are canon code — `packs/<pack>/tasks/<task>/task.mjs` plus the shared vocabulary in [`precondition-policy.mjs`](packs/claudinite-tasks/precondition-policy.mjs) — vendored byte-identical into every member. No member setting can vary a task's gate. The only per-repo knobs are which packs are declared, `taskScheduler.disabledTasks`, and the anchor hours.

So "align across repos" collapses to: *get the canon right once*. I read all 14 members' `.claudinite-settings.json` to confirm that's true in practice, and it is.

## The catalog — 25 tasks, by cadence

| cadence | task | work | gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| daily | `chrome-extension/store-release` | code | `manifest-ahead \|\| substantive-change` ᴸ |
| daily | `claudinite-canon-curation/growth-promote` | **opus** | `fleet-local-packs-changed` ᴸ |
| daily | `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/fleet-pack-seeds` | code | `none` |
| daily | `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/fleet-roster` | code | `none` |
| daily | `claudinite-growth/growth-extract` | **opus** | `substantive-change` |
| daily | `claudinite-growth/logs-prune` | code | `log-past-retention` ᴸ |
| daily | `claudinite-lifecycle/update` | code+sonnet | `none` |
| daily | `claudinite-tasks/task-janitor` | code | `none` |
| daily | `claudinite-tasks/usage-fold` | code | `any-commit \|\| session-captured` |
| daily | `tidy-repo/tidy-issues` | sonnet | `issues-touched` |
| weekly | `basics/ci-performance` | code+sonnet | `substantive-change \|\| prs-touched` |
| weekly | `claudinite-canon-curation/growth-discover-packs` | **opus** | `none` |
| weekly | `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/fleet-add-missing-packs` | code | `none` |
| weekly | `claudinite-growth/growth-dedup` | code+**opus** | `mount-moved \|\| commits-under:.claudinite/local` |
| weekly | `claudinite-growth/prose-to-checks-sweep` | **opus** | `repo-active` |
| weekly | `claudinite-growth/rule-revalidation` | **opus** | `repo-active` |
| weekly | `product-wiki/wiki-growth` | **opus** | `repo-active` && `no-open-pr-touching:product-wiki/` |
| weekly | `tidy-repo/improve-comments` | **opus** | `substantive-change` && `commits-outside:.claudinite/` && `no-open-pr-titled:…` |
| weekly | `tidy-repo/tidy-prs` | sonnet | `prs-touched` |
| monthly | `claudinite-canon-curation/upstream-watch` | **opus** | `none` |
| manual ×5 | `deploy-oauth-exchange`, `fleet-baseline`, `adopt-requested-packs`, `verify-production`, `implement-request` | — | `none` ×4, `request-eligible` ᴸ |

ᴸ = task-local term, in a `preconditions.mjs` beside the declaration (4 of them: `manifest-ahead`, `fleet-local-packs-changed`, `log-past-retention`, `request-eligible`). The other 11 terms are the shared built-ins: `repo-active`, `substantive-change`, `any-commit`, `session-captured`, `issues-touched`, `prs-touched`, `mount-moved`, `commits-under`, `commits-outside`, `no-open-pr-touching`, `no-open-pr-titled`.

## The fleet's settings

| repo | tasks | daily | disabled |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claudinite | 18 | **5** | `claudinite-lifecycle/update` |
| the other 13 | 15–20 | 4 (default) | — |

Both divergences are correct, not drift: the canon has no mount to converge (it *is* the source), and its 05:00 anchor puts `growth-promote` and the curation tasks an hour *after* the fleet's 04:00 converge — which is exactly what they need, since they read members' freshly-converged state.

11 of 13 members sit at `claudinite-tasks` 60902.**2** vs the canon's .**3**. That's the convergence window from PR [#1597](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1597) landing today, not drift — gcec and Shepherd already have .3, the rest pick it up at tonight's 04:00.

## My decision: no precondition changes

I went looking for the two failure shapes the corpus warns about and found neither.

- **Standing state used as a gate** — none. Every movement term reads a window; I checked each `none` against its own in-file rationale and all seven hold. `upstream-watch` and `growth-discover-packs` are the interesting ones: both are ungated *deliberately*, because their subject is a standing opportunity (a technology nobody homes; a practice that moved upstream), and gating standing state is the anti-pattern, not the fix.
- **A gate that never declines** — `usage-fold`'s `any-commit` is true daily on any converging member, so it effectively never declines. That's by design: it deliberately counts task-authored commits because it measures the machinery, and it's code-work, so a run costs seconds.

The one place I'd push if pushed is the three weekly **opus** tasks gated on `repo-active` alone (`prose-to-checks-sweep`, `rule-revalidation`, `wiki-growth`). On a live repo that's true nearly every week, so it's a liveness floor rather than a trigger — which brushes the rule *"a signal true most days should only widen an already-triggered run."* But both headers argue it explicitly, and there is no narrower signal available: the backlogs they work are standing, so there's nothing to widen.

**What's actually missing is evidence, not tuning.** Shepherd's `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` carries a `queue` field family — `done / delivered / obsolete / none`, where `none` *is* the declined-precondition counter — and it is **empty for all 14 members**, folded only through 2026-08-24. Nothing yet reports how often each gate declines. That is precisely what [#1579](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1579) Phase 3 exists to produce, and it returns 2026-09-09.

options.label: Nothing — wait for #1579's reads (Recommended)
options.description: Land no changes. The only real gap is that no decline-rate evidence exists yet; #1579 Phase 3 returns 2026-09-09 with five quoted reads off real anchored runs. Tuning gates before that is guessing.

options.label: Cut the opus spend on the three `repo-active` weeklies
options.description: Narrow prose-to-checks-sweep, rule-revalidation and wiki-growth so they don't fire every Sunday on every live repo. No narrower signal exists today, so this means inventing one (e.g. a backlog-nonempty term) — real design work against no measurement.

options.label: Wire up the missing measurement first
options.description: The `queue` counters (done/delivered/obsolete/`none`) are empty fleet-wide. Find out whether usage-fold is failing to write them or simply has no post-24-Aug data folded yet, and fix it if broken — that's what makes any later tuning evidence-based.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

**Your question:** the whole week, plus an hour of slack. The signal window is the task's own period, not a fixed day — `lookbackMs = periodMs(frequency) + 1h` ([`queue/signals.mjs:15`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/signals.mjs#L15)), and `periodMs` returns 7d for `weekly`, 31d for `monthly`, 24h otherwise ([`queue/anchors.mjs:17-28`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/anchors.mjs#L17-L28)). So a weekly task's `repo-active` asks "was this repo silent for 169 hours", a daily one asks "for 25 hours". The slack exists because a scheduler tick can fire late and a window that ended exactly at the anchor would drop the commits in that gap.

| EdFringeNow | `edfringe/refresh-tickets` | manual | code | `ticketWindow()` — August only, Edinburgh clock |
| GoogleCalendarEventCreator | `gcec/create-extractor` | daily | **sonnet** | eligible `extractor-request` issues, or a touched cached-page file |

Four of the six are `agent_model: 'none'` — pure code, idempotent, deliver nothing when unchanged. Their unconditional `run: true` is correct and argued in place: the inputs (edfringe.com, the canon's counts, other repos' issue lists) leave no trace in the repo, so there is no signal to gate on and the cadence *is* the gate. `create-extractor` is tightly gated. No spend problem in any of them.

**One real defect.** [`generic-extractor-improvements`](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/blob/main/.claudinite/local/packs/gcec/tasks/generic-extractor-improvements/task.mjs) hand-reimplements the built-in `substantive-change` term line for line — same `substantiveChange` read, same sha-slicing, same reason wording. A busy week floods that opus run's scope section. It collapses to `preconditions: ['substantive-change']` — ~20 lines gone and the cap inherited.

All three `repo-active` weeklies work a **standing backlog**, stated in both headers. So a movement gate would starve them: once prose stops changing, `prose-to-checks-sweep` halts with its backlog half-converted. That rules out the obvious lever, leaving two — and they differ in a way your goal doesn't settle.

Also: `wiki-growth` already carries `no-open-pr-touching:product-wiki/`, so it's covered. The target is really two tasks.

Complete answer, and it's clean: **the PR state is read twice, both times live.** The anchor-side ask ([`scheduler-run.mjs:672-700`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/scheduler-run.mjs#L672-L700)) collects signals fresh at the anchor and files the item only on a yes — and an error there **fails open**, so a read it can't make never suppresses a run. The executor then re-evaluates at pick with its own fresh collection, explicitly refusing to trust the anchor verdict forward. Nothing is pre-computed and carried.

The one consequence worth naming: if the previous round's PR is open *at the anchor*, that period is skipped even if the PR merges an hour later — the next ask is the next anchor. That's exactly how `improve-comments` behaves today, so the guard adds no new behaviour class. Proceeding with it on both.
